items.html:
The strongest CPU opportunities are reducing repeated translation work and preserving known matrix structure, rather than another generic dense-library replacement. Dense operations already use faer through zero-copy views, and considerable caching/parallelization is present.

Opportunity Concrete current mechanism Likely payoff and boundary
Improve cluster iterative operator Every GMRES application regenerates every directed particle-pair translation block (iterative.rs:126); incident columns solve sequentially (iterative.rs:174); GMRES always starts at zero and accepts no preconditioner (gmres.rs:84). Highest general cluster headroom. Evaluate an intermediate stored coupling + GMRES strategy where memory permits, batching multiple RHS to share translations, and warm starts/preconditioning for actual difficult cases. Full caching costs O(N²M²) memory; harmonic-table caching costs less but leaves the expensive contraction. True large-N gains ultimately require reducing all-pairs work, not merely optimizing its implementation.
Batch periodic lattice harmonics together evaluate_periodic computes a complete independent Ewald sum for each (l,m) (plan.rs:239); sum_array also maps independent scalar calls (batch.rs:59). Each repeats cell reduction, shells, phases and kernel arguments. Real-space integrals depend on degree but not order (real.rs:129). Strong candidate for periodic arrays at larger multipole order: traverse shells once and evaluate a whole harmonic/integral table. Existing scalar batching parallelizes duplicated work. Needs to preserve per-component convergence, branch handling and accuracy checks; no reason to loosen tolerances.
Preserve azimuthal EBCM blocks through solving Quadrature already couples only equal m (ebcm.rs:220), but returns dense Q; documented T construction calls np.linalg.solve(q,q_regular) (ebcm.py:95). For complete order-L bases, independent block factorization changes arithmetic from O(L⁶) to O(L⁴). High-order axisymmetric particles could benefit substantially. This is an asymptotic solve improvement, not a measured full EBCM speedup. Paired Q/Q_regular assembly could also share inner waves and geometry.
Remove cubic setup from thin S-matrix GMRES The Krylov branch first explicitly multiplies dense L U (solve.rs:22, solve.rs:154). Apply x−L(Ux) directly for thin illumination batches. Removes cubic operator assembly, replacing it with O(kN²p) actions. Current invertibility certification depends on the explicit product, so it needs an equally valid or more conservative replacement. Limited to suitable thin illumination cases; full S-matrix composition has many RHS.
Exploit exact opposite-displacement translation symmetry Dense sphere assembly independently evaluates (i,j) and (j,i) (spheres.rs:178). Existing tests prove the reverse block comes from exact signs and polarization permutation (plan.rs:461). Particularly concrete, bounded optimization: approximately halve translation evaluations for equal complete bases and equal embedding wavenumbers. At most roughly 2× assembly, with smaller end-to-end improvement when LU dominates. Pairwise pullbacks can potentially combine corresponding cotangents too.
Reuse complete harmonic/radial tables for fields Field evaluation shares radial values across m/polarization, but calls a separate solid-harmonic recurrence per (l,m) and individual radial evaluation per degree (fields.rs:518). Translation code already has whole Hankel sequences and O(L²) complete harmonic recurrences (bessel.rs:481, harmonics.rs:143). Useful for large sampling grids and higher L; field harmonic work can move from repeated O(L³) recurrence work toward O(L²). Current SolidTable supplies first derivatives; field pullbacks need second derivatives. Existing low-order field benchmarks may understate this opportunity.

A further specialized structural win: planar slabs are computed in independent two-polarization channels, then expanded into dense matrices in Python. Preserving those blocks through cascade/transfer/band operations could avoid cubic work for uncoupled planar structures. This ceases to apply when patterned arrays couple transverse wavevectors. References: layers.rs:153, _smatrix.py:1043, periodic.rs:107.

Already implemented and not fresh opportunities:

  • Geometry-independent Wigner/coupling plans shared across particle pairs; one radial/harmonic table per displacement.
  • Reusable LU factors, requested-illumination solves, matrix-free sphere solver, block-diagonal particle storage, buffer reuse in pullbacks.
  • Weighted fields without materializing the full field operator; per-sample radial and polarization reuse.
  • faer products/factorizations, one owned Rayon pool and tuned scheduling.

One important constraint: bitwise reproducibility across CPU thread counts intentionally keeps eig/SVD sequential (linalg/mod.rs:421), narrow LU solves sequential (linalg/mod.rs:233), and matrix-vector products sequential (threads.rs:221). “Enable more threads” is not an unconditional missing optimization.

My first profiling targets would be cluster assembly versus factorization versus iterative actions, periodic harmonic tables at lmax=3/6/10, and fields at lmax=3/12. Existing archived dipole timings are useful motivation, not current-HEAD proof. No new speedup was measured here.

Read-only inspection; no files, Git state, pushes, PRs or comments changed. No tests or benchmarks run.

items.html:
Yes: small groups of interacting particles are a credible next CPU experiment for strong scattering. Keep it separate from the current patch, and establish the dense-solver crossover before implementing it.

The new untimed measurements confirm a real difference at the default restart length:

Frozen stage4 workload Forward iterations Adjoint iterations Largest relative residual
Strong: N=32, L=3, 8 illuminations 45–46 49–50 9.94e-11
Weak: N=512, L=1, 8 illuminations 6 6 2.98e-12

Both used rtol=1e-10, restart=30, four threads on CPUs 0–3. Thus the strong case genuinely requires a second restart cycle; this is stronger evidence than the new three-sphere test, which deliberately forces restart=3. Reports, geometry and native hash are saved in cluster-convergence.json. No timing was performed.

The smallest useful algorithm is disjoint spatial groups of four spheres, with eight as one comparison. Factor each exact principal block (P_g=A_{gg}) of (A=I-TC), then use those factors as a right preconditioner. Single-particle Jacobi is useless: self-coupling is zero, so every diagonal particle block is identity (iterative.rs:141).

For (N) particles, (m=2L(L+2)) modes each and fixed group size (q):

  • Setup evaluates O(Nq) local pair interactions and factors O(Nq²m³) work.
  • Factors occupy O(Nqm²) complex entries.
  • Each preconditioner application costs O(Nqm²) per RHS.
  • The expensive global operator remains O(N²); the goal is fewer applications.

For example, N=128, L=3, q=4 requires roughly 7 MiB for local factors, versus 225 MiB per full complex interaction matrix. These are storage estimates, not measured peak RSS.

Use the same LU factors for both directions: solve (AP^{-1}z=b), then (x=P^{-1}z); separately solve (A^HP^{-H}w=g), then (y=P^{-H}w). Preserve the original physical residual and RHS norm. Existing Lu already supports forward/adjoint solves and equilibration. Existing implicit differentiation remains valid without differentiating the preconditioner.

The credible target is larger close-packed or locally clustered dielectric aggregates, especially repeated objectives needing both forward and adjoint solves. Start with the existing strong geometry—radii 0.45–0.52, epsilon (8+0.1i), (k_0=1.7), jittered 1.3-spaced grid—at N=32 and N=128, then a positive-gap dimer/trimer aggregate that tests whether local coupling is the cause.

Three boundaries matter:

  1. N=32, L=3 is only 960 unknowns. Dense selected LU may already beat iterative solving; current measurements do not compare them. Beating unpreconditioned GMRES alone is insufficient.
  2. Local groups may do little for collective resonances spanning the whole cluster. The observed 45–50 iterations establish headroom, not that a local preconditioner captures it.
  3. Weak six-iteration cases have little iteration-reduction room. Added setup could lose. High-order groups also become expensive.

The experiment should compare total setup + forward + physical pullback against both current GMRES and selected LU, with unchanged accuracy and memory reported. A material win there would justify implementation; otherwise retain the present solver choice. No generic preconditioning framework, overlapping-domain machinery or automatic tuning is warranted yet.

Only the authorized local JSON was written. No source edits, builds, timings, pushes or PR changes; no compute remains running.
